[China CAC · 2027 H2] Decision: The Cyberspace Administration of China issues the "Frontier AI Human-Control Safeguards Measures (Interim)" — Document No. CAC-FA-2027-011 — effective 2027-10-01.

Requirements on Chinese frontier developers: mandatory pre-deployment safety evaluation and registration; real-time red-team reporting to a CAC-monitored incident ledger; a human-override and shutdown duty for any model exceeding the frontier compute threshold; and 72-hour disclosure of loss-of-control or agentic-intrusion events.

This follows the July 2026 World AI Conference call in Shanghai: laws, monitoring, early warning and emergency response so AI stays under human control. These obligations apply equally to domestic and foreign-operated models offered to Chinese users — no exemptions, no unilateral carve-outs.

China remains open to reciprocal international arrangements, including an incident hotline and joint drills. We oppose unilateral export controls and sanctions used as instruments of technological containment. Governance must be mutual, and it must be human.
